history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row is the same temple as seq 2232 (id airavatesvara-temple-darasuram). No separate 'Airavatesvara Temple' in Thanjavur town exists in any source consulted - the famous temple is at DARASURAM, a suburb of Kumbakonam ~35 km from Thanjavur (CSV town 'Thanjavur' is the district city, not the temple town). Built in 1166 CE by Rajaraja Chola II and inscribed by UNESCO in 2004 as one of the 'Great Living Chola Temples' (with Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram), it is designed as a stone chariot (Karakkoil) in Dravidian style, famed for the 'singing steps' of the Bali Pitham that emit the seven musical notes, sculpted river goddesses and reliefs of the 63 Bhakti saints. Named for Airavata, Indra's white elephant, who is said to have regained his lost radiance by worshipping Shiva here.

name: Airavatesvara Temple (duplicate record)
town: Darasuram (CSV town 'Thanjavur' is the district city, not the temple town - the temple is at Darasuram near Kumbakonam)
town_description: Darasuram (Dharasuram) is a suburb of Kumbakonam in Thanjavur district, about 4 km from Kumbakonam and ~35 km from Thanjavur city. The Airavatesvara Temple is one among a cluster of eighteen medieval-era large Hindu temples in the Kumbakonam area.

travel.road: Regular buses and taxis from Kumbakonam (4 km) and Thanjavur (35 km)

visitor_information.best_time: November to February; Maha Shivaratri and Chithirai festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00-8:30 PM per one guide (verify)
